messages:
incident-bot: [ALERT] prod-west-1 KV cache metadata growth + continuous-batch spikes — 6xx rate rising, token latency p95 > 1.2s. Auto-notify to #incidents.

maria (oncall): I'm on it. @shawn can you grab logs + current batch config? I want customer impact assessment.

shawn: looking. early signs: continuous batching enabled on several services, batch size jump from 16->64 around 09:12 UTC. KV block manager reported lots of small block allocations, high metadata churn.

maria (oncall): thx. can we hard-limit continuous batch size to 8 for prod-west as a quick mitigation?

shawn: we can patch config now. prepping kubectl patch for inference-router configmap.

ops-bot: deploy started: patch configmap inference-router-prod-west (shard-3) by shawn at 09:18 UTC.

shawn: patch applied. snippet: ```yaml
continuousBatching:
  enabled: true
  maxBatchSize: 8
  interArrivalMs: 10
```

maria (oncall): rolling restart routers to pick up config. rolling 1/5 done. watching metrics.

prod-support: customer "acme-inc" reported latency spikes and errors on embed endpoint since ~09:10 UTC. They called support. flagging for SRE / CS.

elaine: taking customer comms. sending proactive note: we are mitigating an infrastructure degradation affecting embedding latency in prod-west; will update in 30m.

shawn: after config change, p95 token latency dropped from 1.2s -> 420ms within 2 minutes. 5xx rate falling. KV metadata allocation rate down ~70%.

maria (oncall): good. mitigation working. need to understand root cause. early hypothesis: block size tuning plus continuous-batching interplay causing many small block allocations and metadata expansion — leads to GC-like pauses and perf cliff.

dave: I saw related logs: block-manager eviction loop spending CPU in walkMetadata for dense small writes. snippet: ```logs
[09:11:23] blockmgr: allocated block id=0x7ff size=4k
[09:11:23] blockmgr: metadata entries ++ count=8123 -> 16412
```

maria (oncall): ok can we roll a targeted hotfix to backstop metadata growth: add a circuit-breaker that rejects non-urgent continuous batches above 16 items and increment block compaction frequency? we need a short-term patch for all regions.

shawn: will open PR for runtime config + patch to block-manager thresholds. PR: https://git.internal/r/redwood/runtime/pulls/6892 (WIP). Planning hotpatch rollout after review.

ops-bot: canary rollout scheduled to prod-west shard-3 in 10 minutes.

maria (oncall): handoff: I need to go offline for a dependency meeting in 10m. @elaine you're lead for customer comms and post-mit triage. @shawn continue infra mitigation and postmortem note. If anything regresses, @dave escalate to eng-runtime.

elaine: acknowledged. I'll keep the channel updated and coordinate with CS. Draft sent to ACME.

shawn: canary applied to shard-3. telemetry shows compaction frequency up, metadata growth stabilizing. will expand to other shards in controlled bursts.

prod-support: acme replied: "Thanks for quick response. Latency back to normal for us." marking impacted as HIGH priority but no data loss.

maria (oncall): thanks team. action items: 1) roll hotfix to all regions (shawn) 2) post-incident analysis on block sizing and eviction heuristics (dave + eng-runtime) 3) update runbook to include circuit-breaker for continuous batching (maria + eng-sre) 4) follow-up with ACME (elaine).

elaine: noted. scheduling customer follow-up call for 16:00 UTC.

shawn: expanding rollout now. will monitor for 30m.

incident-bot: incident resolved: metrics OK for 15m, severity lowered to advisory. Incident duration: ~28m.

maria (oncall): handing off to eng-runtime for deeper RCA. Leaving channel. Thanks all :thumbsup:."
